data.title: BOJ's Ueda Reaffirms Readiness to Keep Raising Rates
Asian Equities Decline as Caution Prevails
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities were broadly lower Thursday morning as firmed expectations of higher interest rates inspired little demand for stocks and sentiment stayed cautious.

Investors are digesting hawkish-sounding minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, and looking ahead to the trilateral summit between U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Trump and Xi are also scheduled for a separate bilateral meeting. The meetings represent the highest-level diplomatic engagement in months and will be closely watched for any signals on trade, technology restrictions, and the broader geopolitical framework affecting Asian markets," Commerzbank Research analysts said.

Anthropic's trading debut is also in focus, seen as a major test of appetite for artificial-intelligence trades after the Nvidia scandal sparked another wave of selloffs in the technology sector.

Concerns about the impact of tightened U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continue to weigh on tech and AI-related stocks in Asia.

Fragile risk sentiment was evident across major indexes.

South Korea's Kospi gave up early gains to turn lower during the morning session, and was recently down 0.9%. Taiwan's Taiex was off by 2.7%, while Chinese benchmarks were in the red. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average swung between gains and losses and was last 0.1% higher.

In Hong Kong, major tech names posted sharp drops, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index 2.1% lower.

Elsewhere, crude oil futures were mixed after Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday, while continuing attacks against ships seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate futures edged 0.1% lower to $83.15 a barrel and front-month Brent rose 0.3% to $92.21 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Gold recovered some ground, rising 0.7%, but stayed around its lowest levels in over on year at $3,750.18 an ounce. Silver also bounced back but stayed weak.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

data.title: Saudi Aramco issues latest fuel oil tender for end-November and December loading, sources say
data.description:
Saudi Aramco has issued its latest tender to sell high-sulphur fuel oil for loading in late November and December, trade sources said on Thursday.

It offered 11 HSFO cargoes in the latest tender issued late on Wednesday, including seven cargoes for loading from Ras Tanura and four for loading from Jubail. The tender will close on November 23.

data.title: India bonds seen flat as traders await fresh rate cues, debt supply
data.description:
By Dharamraj Dhutia

Indian government bonds are expected to be little changed in early trading on Thursday as traders look for fresh cues on the interest-rate outlook, while awaiting debt supply due a day later.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yield is expected to move between 7.26% and 7.32%, according to a private bank trader, after ending at 7.2858% on Wednesday.

"With yesterday's attempt of taking the yield sustainably below 7.25% thwarted, we should see some consolidation in 7.30%-7.32% range," the trader said.

Shorter-dated US Treasury yields rose after minutes from the Federal Reserve's latest meeting showed support for holding rates steady was less broad than the headline 10-2 vote suggested.

"The prospect of a 50bp hike in December was already being raised and has since become more likely following stronger-than-expected payrolls and inflation figures," Capital Economics said in a note.

Treasury yields have stabilised for now, but saw a large upswing last week, with markets fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Fed in December, following stronger-than-expected October inflation data and hawkish comments from US Fed officials.

Crude prices remained steady, but the outlook is still fragile as any prolonged disruption to tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz could quickly tighten global supplies.

This remains a risk for energy import-dependent India, as it affects current account deficit pressures, the local currency, and inflation.

The market has been positioned for another Reserve Bank of India rate hike in early December, after India's retail inflation moved above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance threshold for the first time in two years.

Meanwhile, New Delhi will sell bonds worth 330 billion rupees ($3.53 billion) on Friday, which includes the liquid five-year security.

RATES

Overnight index swap rates are also expected to consolidate around current levels.

On Wednesday, the one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate ended at 6.5250%, the two-year rate (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) closed at 6.52%, and the liquid five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate settled at 6.56%.

($1 = 93.4700 Indian rupees)

data.title: Oil prices steady as supply surplus softens sentiment though Gulf war supports
data.description:
By Colleen Howe

Oil prices were steady on Thursday after falling previously as increasing expectations for a supply surplus and higher interest rates softened sentiment, outweighing support from attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the lingering Iran war.

Brent crude futures were trading up 17 cents, or 0.18%, at $92.12 a barrel as of 0237 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 9 cents, or 0.11%, to $83.17.

Brent fell 1.3% in the previous session while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels.

Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates that would cause lower economic growth and slower demand increases for oil. That would also strengthen the dollar, raising prices for non-US buyers paying for dollar-denominated crude in different currencies.

Minutes from the US Federal Reserve's October meeting, released on Wednesday, bolstered investor expectations that the central bank could raise interest rates at its next meeting in December to control inflation.

"Softer oil prices provide some relief to those concerned about persistent inflationary pressures, although the question is no longer simply whether the Fed will hike rates in December, but by how much. This, in turn, supports the dollar, hindering any attempt by the oil market to rally," analysts at PVM, a brokerage, said in a note dated November 18.

A larger-than-expected rise in US oil stocks reported on Wednesday also weighed on the market outlook.

US crude inventories rose by 3.4 million barrels to 417.8 million barrels in the week ended November 13, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a rise of 58,000 barrels.

Still, risks remain for Middle East oil supply amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

Iran's navy said three oil tankers sailing east of the Strait of Hormuz were disabled by mines, Iranian media reported on Wednesday.

Markets are awaiting the trilateral summit between the leaders of the US, China and Russia, seeking clues about the prospects of a negotiated end to the US-Iran war and Russia's invasion of Ukraine, which have disrupted global oil markets.

Reuters reported on Wednesday that Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries' combined crude processing volumes by 45% since late October, citing industry sources.

data.title: Global commodity prices plunge: These are the metals impacted and Emkay's preferred plays
data.description:
Global commodity markets are experiencing a broad sell-off as a surging US Dollar, mounting Federal Reserve rate hike expectations, and an unwinding of the artificial intelligence infrastructure trade pressure prices across energy, metals, and agriculture.

With the US Dollar Index climbing to a 19-month high on the back of rising inflation and higher US yields, markets are now pricing in a greater than 90% probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December 2026.

Crude Oil Prices At Three-Month Low

In the energy market, Brent crude oil prices have dropped to a three-month low, holding near $92 per barrel after tumbling 20% in November alone. Bearish sentiment has been compounded by supply-side pressures, with the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) estimating a 2 million barrels-per-day surplus in Q2 2026. Reinforcing these oversupply concerns, US crude inventories jumped by 3.38 million barrels alongside simultaneous increases in US gasoline and distillate stocks.

Base Metals Impacted

The sharpest declines have hit the metals complex, particularly base metals tied to AI infrastructure buildouts. Despite Nvidia posting strong earnings, its signal toward greater discipline in AI portfolio investments has prompted investors to unwind long positions in the AI trade.

Combined with a sluggish demand backdrop in China, copper prices plunged 5.4% overnight to hit a seven-month low. Prices are now down 13% for the month, thereby wiping out its gains to turn flat for 2026.

Similarly, aluminum slid to a 52-week low after falling 7% in November, while zinc dropped 5% overnight, though it still holds onto a 13% gain for the year. Tin also fell to an eight-month low, declining 8% this month even as exchange inventories tighten, with LME stocks hovering near a one-year low of 3,885 tons and Shanghai inventories down 66% from June to 4,000 tons.

Gold, Silver Sell-Off Continues

Precious and industrial metals have not been spared from the dollar rally and shifting demand trends either. Gold prices fell 3.2% overnight to the lowest since September 2025, bringing its year-to-date decline to 13%, while silver tumbled 4.8% overnight to a 14-month low. The white metal is now down 36% in 2026.

Platinum shed 4.25%, and palladium sank to a 19-month low below $1,000 per ounce as an 8% year-on-year rise in global electric vehicle sales in October 2026 continues to weigh on traditional automotive catalyst demand.

Meanwhile, soft and agricultural commodities followed the broader downward trend, with wheat down 4%, cotton and cocoa losing 3% each, corn hitting 14-week lows, and sugar falling to a two-month low—leaving rice futures as a rare outlier near 2024 highs.

What Next For Metals & Top Stock Picks

Looking at the domestic sector outlook, analysts see diverging fortunes for Indian metals.

Under a bear-case scenario of aluminum and alumina prices at $2,600 and $360 per ton respectively, Emkay prefers Vedanta Aluminium with a fair value of ₹449 (at 6x EV/EBITDA), notes limited upside of 7.2% for Hindalco, and ranks NALCO as its least-preferred pick with a fair value of ₹326.

Conversely, domestic steelmakers appear better insulated; safeguard duties and localized pricing dynamics—with HSBC noting domestic steel trades at a 5% to 6% premium over Chinese imports—position the sector for strong volume growth in the second half of FY27 as domestic demand improves.

Axis Capital notes that global aluminum demand growth slowed to 1.2% year-on-year in the first nine months of 2026, compared to a 3% CAGR between 2023 and 2025, projecting the global market to swing into a 0.5 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) surplus in 2027.

The Nifty metal index was the worst performing index on Wednesday, falling over 2.5%, with nearly all constituents ending the session with losses led by Vedanta Aluminium, which fell 5.5%.

data.title: How safe is your job? Aus economy sheds 43,500 jobs as unemployment hits four-year high
data.description:
Key points:
  • Australia's unemployment rate has risen for three straight months, from 4.5% in July to 4.9% in October – its highest level since October 2021 and a far cry from the labour shortages of the post-pandemic recovery.
  • October's Labour Force survey showed 43,500 jobs lost against economists' forecasts for a 25,000 gain – the second large monthly fall in a row – with part-time workers and young Australians bearing the brunt.
  • We look at where the job losses are falling, why ASX consumer stocks have been warning of exactly this, what the major investment banks expect next, and what it all means for the RBA's December meeting.

For most of the post-Covid period, the labour market was the Australian economy's strongest pillar. Recent data suggests that pillar is cracking. Over the 12 months to October, the number of unemployed Australians rose by 95,400, or 14.5%, while employment grew by just 83,500 – meaning more people joined the jobless queue than found work.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' (ABS) Labour Force survey released today showed seasonally adjusted employment fell by 43,500 in October, well short of economists' forecasts for a 25,000 increase. It follows September's 36,400 decline, and pushed the unemployment rate to 4.9%, with 753,700 Australians now looking for work.

In this article, we unpack who’s losing their jobs, how corporate Australia has been flagging the slowdown for weeks, and what the economists at the major investment banks expect from here – including what today's numbers could mean for the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA).

Part-timers first in the firing line

Part-time employment fell by 40,600 in October, while full-time employment slipped by just 2,900. September told the same story: full-time jobs rose by 35,400 while part-time jobs fell by 71,800. Across the two months, that's roughly 112,000 part-time positions gone against a net gain of around 32,500 full-time roles.

Consider that the Australian economy has shed jobs in three of the last four months, and the chart below appears to show a sharp downturn since July (i.e., following the first three of five RBA official cash rate hikes this year).

Australia: monthly change in employment (seasonally adjusted). Source: ABS Labour Force, Australia, October 2026 (seasonally adjusted)

Hours worked fell 0.2% and the participation rate eased to 66.6%. Fewer hours worked means there’s less work to go around – a leading indicator that employers are pulling back on their labour requirements. A falling participation rate, meanwhile, suggests more Australians are becoming discouraged about finding work and stepping out of the jobs market altogether.

Youth unemployment rose to 11.3% from 11.1%, the highest since October 2021, signalling that younger workers are taking the hardest hit. Consider that jobs for new entrants to the workforce are typically the first to go at the beginning of a protracted downturn in hiring.

Corporate Australia saw this coming

ASX companies have been sending a signal for months now that the local economy is beginning to bear the brunt of higher interest rates and a sharp downturn in consumer confidence.

Nick Scali (NCK) told the market on 21 October that Australia-NZ written sales orders fell 15% in the first quarter of FY27, with store traffic down about 10%. The furniture retailer expects first-half revenue for the region to land 11–14% below the prior year.

JB Hi-Fi (JBH) reported a 1.4% fall in comparable sales at JB Hi-Fi Australia for the September quarter, and said sales had slowed in October ahead of Black Friday and Christmas. Customers, it said, remain focused on value and are increasingly holding out for promotional events.

Eagers Automotive (APE) said on 5 November that third-quarter trading in Australia was hit by industry-wide headwinds, citing the elevated interest rate environment, persistent inflationary pressures and higher fuel prices. APE still expects record revenue for calendar 2026, largely on the back of acquisitions.

There are many more. The problem facing Aussie retailers is that margins are being squeezed from both ends. Just yesterday, the ABS reported the wage price index rose 3.5% over the year to the September quarter, above expectations according to Macquarie, which notes the result was largely driven by the Fair Work Commission's 4.75% award wage increase.

Meanwhile, UBS's reading of the latest business confidence survey showed selling prices easing to 2.4% annualised in October while purchase costs remain very high – which the investment bank says implies significant margin compression.

What the experts are saying

Macquarie also noted that SEEK job ad volumes were down 6% year-on-year in October, while applications per ad hit a record 239 in September – i.e., fewer jobs, and more people chasing what’s there. Looking forward, the bank sees limited evidence of a sustained recovery in ad volumes, pointing to weakening business confidence and rising unemployment.

Morgan Stanley, in its 2027 outlook for the Australian economy released this week, expects sticky core inflation to keep the RBA cash rate on hold at 4.85% through the first half of 2027, before rising unemployment creates enough slack for two rate cuts before year’s end.

UBS is on the same page regarding the next rate cut – tipping November 2027. Its analysts believe rates may ease 50 basis points from there, but they caution that risks are now shifting towards an earlier or larger round of cuts, given the sharper-than-expected housing downturn and rapidly weakening consumer and business sentiment.

What to watch next

Today's data is a sobering reminder that the economy is entering a dangerous phase – inflation still well above the RBA's 2–3% target, a labour market shedding jobs, and growth slowing. UBS expects October's monthly CPI to show headline inflation at a new cycle high of 4.7% year-on-year, suggesting the inflation picture is likely to worsen still.

That CPI print is due on 25 November (next Wednesday), and markets will be watching it closely. Then, we’ll have the RBA's December meeting on 8 December and November's Labour Force data on 17 December to round out the year. A third consecutive fall of the size seen in September and October would certainly get the RBA’s attention – and would make it harder for Treasurer Jim Chalmers to argue, as he did after September’s numbers, that the labour market “remains resilient and one of our greatest strengths”.

References: This article draws on the ABS Labour Force, Australia, October 2026 release (19 November 2026) and the ABS Labour Force, Australia, September 2026 release (15 October 2026); ASX announcements from Nick Scali (Trading Update and 1H FY27 Profit Guidance, 21 October 2026), JB Hi-Fi (FY27 Sales Update, 29 October 2026) and Eagers Automotive (Trading Update, 5 November 2026); and broker research from Macquarie (Australian Wages Growth, 18 November 2026; Australian job ad volumes, 18 November 2026), Morgan Stanley (2027 Australia Macro+ Outlook, 16 November 2026) and UBS (Australian Economic Comment, 10 and 13 November 2026).

data.title: Singapore Tourism Likely to Stay Weak This Year — Market Talk

data.title: Australia's Job Market In Worse State Than Thought — Market Talk
data.description: After five interest rate increases this year by the Reserve Bank of Australia, economists have been waiting for the economy to break. With unemployment jumping to its highest level since 2021 in October, it was more of a crack than a snap. The job market looks worse than what the RBA anticipated, says Taylor Nugent, economist at NAB. The trend in employment growth is now just 7,000 per month, well below what is required to keep up with population growth, he says. NAB is forecasting a peak in the unemployment rate of 5.5%, compared to the RBA's forecast of 5.1%. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)

data.title: Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd Announces Execution of MEP Equipment Supply and Installation Contracts for Phase 1B of Indonesia Data Center
data.description:
TAICHUNG, Taiwan, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd (the “Company”) today announced that on November 13, 2026, its Indonesian operating subsidiary, PT AGCC AITECH INDONESIA (the “Indonesian Subsidiary”), entered into two definitive contracts with separate contractors for the mechanical, electrical and plumbing (“MEP”) works for Phase 1B of the Company’s planned AGCC-JKT01 data center in West Java, Indonesia (the “Data Center”): an equipment supply agreement for the procurement and supply of MEP equipment (the “Supply Contract”) and an installation works contract for the installation of the MEP equipment and systems (the “Installation Contract” and, together with the Supply Contract, the “Contracts”). The Contracts are in addition to the letters of award for the MEP equipment and installation works for Phase 1A of the Data Center previously announced by the Company on September 1, 2026.

The aggregate contract price under the Contracts is in a range between US$60 million and US$65 million, exclusive of Indonesian value-added tax. Each Contract is priced on a fixed lump-sum basis and is subject to adjustment only as provided in the relevant Contract, including for variations instructed by the Indonesian Subsidiary. The contract prices are denominated in U.S. dollars and are payable in Indonesian Rupiah at the Bank Indonesia middle rate on the relevant invoice date.

The Contracts provide for delivery of the equipment and completion of the installation works during 2027, in accordance with the milestones set out in the Contracts. Each Contract provides for liquidated damages for delay, subject to a cap, and for a defects notification period following taking-over of the installed works. The Indonesian Subsidiary may terminate either Contract for convenience on notice, subject to payment for work performed and other costs reasonably incurred by the relevant contractor.

The Contracts relate to the construction of the Data Center and do not themselves generate revenue. Completion of Phase 1B and commencement of operations at the Data Center remain subject to, among other things, performance by the contractors engaged by the Company and its subsidiaries (the “Group”), completion of related construction and power supply works, availability of funding and applicable regulatory approvals. The Contracts do not by themselves guarantee successful completion of Phase 1B or of the Data Center, or operational capacity, customer utilization, revenue, profitability or positive cash flow.

About Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd

Agencia Comercial Spirits Ltd is a Nasdaq-listed company with two principal business focuses: (i) its established premium whisky operations; and (ii) the development of AI computing infrastructure and cloud-based computing services. These two lines of business represent the Company’s primary operational pillars, with the Company dedicating substantial resources to the development and scaling of its AI computing infrastructure business. The Company’s whisky operations include procurement and distribution of bottled whisky, procurement and distribution of raw cask whisky, and cask-to-bottle and distribution services, including brand-authorized bottling, packaging and sales, in Taiwan and select international markets.

Since early 2026, the Company has launched and been developing its AI Computing Infrastructure Initiative through subsidiaries in Singapore, Indonesia and other jurisdictions. This initiative represents a principal business focus, backed by substantive contractual arrangements for commercial AI computing cloud services and the development of supporting data center, power, network and technical infrastructure. The Company’s historical operating revenue has been derived from its whisky operations, and the AI computing business remains in development and deployment and is subject to significant business, financing, construction, technology, regulatory, customer demand and execution risks.

data.title: Standard Chartered, StraitsX, OCBC complete trial of tokenized deposit interoperability
data.description:
StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered have completed a proof-of-concept examining interoperability between tokenized deposit networks issued by different banks.

According to the press release, the POC was conducted under the Monetary Authority of Singapore's BLOOM initiative, a public-private collaborative project to develop future payment settlement infrastructure.

The examination tested a shared model where StraitsX's settlement infrastructure coordinated payments between OCBC's and Standard Chartered's separate tokenized deposit ecosystems.

"Tokenized deposits have the potential to enable near-instant and programmable money movement, but their broader utility will depend on how effectively different banking ecosystems can connect," said Tianwei Liu, CEO and co-founder of StraitsX. "We are exploring how shared settlement infrastructure can support that interoperability while reducing the need for bilateral arrangements and prefunded liquidity between individual participants."

Interoperability

The companies pointed out that tokenized deposits currently represent claims solely against their issuing banks and therefore cannot move directly between ecosystems that may use different platforms or standards.

The POC addressed this issue by coordinating payment initiation, compliance screening, liquidity checks, settlement and confirmation across the two banks' systems. This arrangement reduced the need for bilateral prefunding compared with conventional models, the release said.

While tokenized deposits enable around-the-clock deposit transfers, the companies pointed out that different ecosystems need to be aligned to fully unlock that potential.

In controlled tests, the parties completed U.S. dollar payment flows outside standard banking hours, demonstrating that interoperable infrastructure could allow "always-on" value transfer across different ecosystems within minutes.

Any further development, as well as commercial implementation, would require assessment of legal, regulatory, operational and commercial arrangements, including settlement finality, liquidity management, participant responsibilities and financial-crime controls, the companies said.

StraitsX holds a Major Payment Institution license under the MAS and issues the XSGD and XUSD stablecoins. OCBC is Singapore’s longest-established bank and the second-largest financial services group in Southeast Asia by assets.

data.title: Asian Equities Decline as Caution Prevails
data.description:
By Ronnie Harui

Asian equities were broadly lower Thursday morning as firmed expectations of higher interest rates inspired little demand for stocks and sentiment stayed cautious.

Investors are digesting hawkish-sounding minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting, and looking ahead to the trilateral summit between U.S. President Donald Trump, China's Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Trump and Xi are also scheduled for a separate bilateral meeting. The meetings represent the highest-level diplomatic engagement in months and will be closely watched for any signals on trade, technology restrictions, and the broader geopolitical framework affecting Asian markets," Commerzbank Research analysts said.

Anthropic's trading debut is also in focus, seen as a major test of appetite for artificial-intelligence trades after the Nvidia scandal sparked another wave of selloffs in the technology sector.

Concerns about the impact of tightened U.S. export restrictions on advanced chips continue to weigh on tech and AI-related stocks in Asia.

Fragile risk sentiment was evident across major indexes.

South Korea's Kospi gave up early gains to turn lower during the morning session, and was recently down 0.9%. Taiwan's Taiex was off by 2.7%, while Chinese benchmarks were in the red. Japan's Nikkei Stock Average swung between gains and losses and was last 0.1% higher.

In Hong Kong, major tech names posted sharp drops, dragging the Hang Seng Tech Index 2.1% lower.

Elsewhere, crude oil futures were mixed after Iran launched strikes against Kuwait and Bahrain on Wednesday, while continuing attacks against ships seeking to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway through which one-fifth of the world's oil is transported.

Front-month West Texas Intermediate futures edged 0.1% lower to $83.15 a barrel and front-month Brent rose 0.3% to $92.21 a barrel, ICE data showed.

Gold recovered some ground, rising 0.7%, but stayed around its lowest levels in over on year at $3,750.18 an ounce. Silver also bounced back but stayed weak.

Write to Ronnie Harui at ronnie.harui@wsj.com

data.title: London copper ticks higher from seven-month trough
data.description:
London copper prices nudged higher on Thursday after hitting their weakest level in seven months the previous session, while Shanghai copper prices continued to fall.

Benchmark three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was up 1.3% to $12,636.50 a metric ton by 0200 GMT after hitting its lowest level since April 7 in the previous session. Wednesday's percentage drop in copper, used in the power and construction sectors, was its biggest one-day decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump was rolling out global tariffs.

The most-traded copper contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SCFv1) was down 4.1% to 95,740 yuan($14,358.99) a ton.

"The current move in LME copper prices looks more like relief than a decisive turn. The sharp retreat was driven by a buoyant US dollar and growing question marks over the pace of the AI data-center buildout, where copper is a key input in the infrastructure," said Tim Waterer, chief market analyst at KCM Trade.

"The main factors to watch remain the path of the dollar, any further signals on AI-related capital spending, and Chinese demand indicators."

Asian equities rose after Claude chatbox maker Anthropic scored the biggest IPO ever with an $81 billion offering ahead of its market debut in a test for the AI trade that has been under pressure in recent weeks.

The dollar hovered near a 19-month high after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments pointed to further US rate hikes. A stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated metals more expensive for holders of other currencies, while higher interest rates can weigh on growth-sensitive commodities such as copper by slowing economic activity.

Among other LME metals, aluminium rose 1.2%, zinc firmed 1.5%, lead added 0.1%, nickel held steady and tin gained 0.6%.

On the SHFE, aluminium (SAFv1) fell 1.3%, zinc (SZNv1) declined 2.7%, lead (SPBv1) lost 0.3%, nickel (SNIv1) slipped 3% and tin (SSNv1) dipped 2.1%.

Data from the International Lead and Zinc Study Group showed that the global lead and zinc markets swung to a deficit in September.

($1 = 6.6676 Chinese yuan renminbi)

data.title: Commodity Corner: Oil steady amid US-Iran tensions; gold rebounds from 14-month low
data.description:
Commodity markets traded higher on November 19, with crude oil prices steady as investors assessed the outlook for the US-Iran conflict and the possibility of fresh attacks on Tehran. Meanwhile, gold recovered from a 14-month low as dip buying provided support despite growing expectations of a potential US Federal Reserve interest rate hike.

Oil steadied as traders assessed the outlook for the US-Iran conflict, including the possibility of fresh attacks against Tehran.

Brent held near $92 a barrel after losing 1.3% on Wednesday, while West Texas Intermediate was above $83.

Gold climbed from a 14-month low as dip buyers helped cushion growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates.

Bullion gained as much as 0.8% to near $3,755 an ounce, recovering some of a 3.2% decline Wednesday that dragged the

metal to its lowest close since September 2025.

Among other precious metals, silver gained 1.6% to $45.79 an ounce, after sinking nearly 5% in the previous session to its lowest close since September 2025. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

The US dollar hovered near a 19-month high on Thursday after Federal Reserve meeting minutes and hawkish comments from a Fed official pointed to further interest rate hikes.

The dollar index was roughly flat at 103.81 in early Asia trade, hovering near its highest level since April 2025.

data.title: Talisker Provides Ore Sorter Facility Construction Update for the Bralorne Gold Project
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 18, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Talisker Resources Ltd. ("Talisker" or the "Company") (TSX: TSK, OTCQX: TSKFF) is pleased to provide an update on the continued advancement of its ore sorter facility (“Sorting Facility”) at the Company’s 100% owned Bralorne Gold Project (“Bralorne”). Construction and engineering activities have continued to advance according to plan, with several major project milestones already completed and a number of critical work programs now entering the execution phase.

Key Highlights:

  • Initial operation of the Sorting Facility is targeted for Q2 2027, with full commissioning expected in July-August 2027.
  • Electrical infrastructure is completed and targeted for commissioning by the end of November 2026, providing power for the future operation of the Sorting Facility.
  • Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorting Facility were successfully completed in September.
  • Phase 2 earthworks and concrete foundation construction is planned to commence late November 2026, following removal of legacy infrastructure.
  • Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) of the TOMRA XRT Sorter is scheduled for early December 2026, with the ore sorter expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.
  • Major long-lead equipment procurement is substantially complete, with the jaw crusher, cone crusher, vibrating screen plant received in Bralorne in October, conveyors, compressors, and buildings being delivered in phases starting December 2026.
  • Construction and mechanical installation activities are planned throughout Q1 2027, supported by completion of detailed engineering and issuance of the remaining construction tender packages in December 2026.

Phase 1 earthworks associated with the electrical infrastructure required to support the Sorter Facility was successfully completed in September. The electrical infrastructure has been procured and installed, with final commissioning scheduled for the end of November 2026. The Mustang Mine power generation and distribution system consists of two 1.5 MW diesel generators, providing a total installed generation capacity of 3 MW at 600 V. The generators can operate in parallel or independently, providing redundancy and backup capability.

Power for the underground mining operations is stepped up to 4.16 kV through a 3,200 kVA transformer and distributed to underground substations that will supply mining equipment.

Surface power distribution is installed and ready to serve the sorting and crushing facilities, as well as supporting all other surface infrastructure requirements. The electrical system incorporates protective switchgear, circuit breakers, ground-fault monitoring, and neutral grounding resistors to ensure safe and reliable operation during the next phase of project development. The power plant and distribution network have also been designed to accommodate the future addition of a third generator unit, allowing for straightforward expansion of site power capacity as operational requirements increase.

As part of the ore sorter site preparation activities, a legacy electrical system located within the planned Sorting Facility footprint has been safely dismantled and removed, clearing part of the area for Phase 2 Earthworks construction. In parallel, the Company has completed construction of a new tension-fabric steel frame heavy-duty mechanic shop and is currently transitioning operations from the legacy shop. Demolition of the former shop is expected to be completed in November, fully opening the sorter site for Phase 2 Earthworks before the end of November.

The Phase 2 Earthworks and concrete contractor is scheduled to mobilize to site in November, marking the beginning of a major construction phase. This work will include cut-and-fill activities, foundation preparation, and pre-cast concrete installation within the area previously occupied by the legacy electrical infrastructure and mechanic shop.

Detailed engineering for the project continues to progress well. Issue-for-Tender packages covering the remaining construction components including equipment installation, electrical and mechanical are expected to be completed in December 2026, positioning the project for construction execution through the first half of 2027.

Procurement efforts have been highly successful, with all major equipment purchased. Equipment is either in manufacturing or pending delivery. A proactive approach to early procurement has significantly de-risked the project schedule and supports the Company's objective of maintaining construction momentum throughout the coming months.

A key milestone will occur during the second week of December when the Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) is conducted for the TOMRA XRT sorter. Following successful testing, the ore sorter is expected to arrive in Canada in January 2027.

The crushing circuit has also reached an important milestone, with all major crushing equipment including the jaw crusher, cone crusher, and vibrating screen plant, now delivered and in Bralorne. The compressor system required to support sorter operations is expected to ship for delivery in January 2027.

Building fabrication remains on track, with the manufacturing of two tension-fabric steel frame buildings completed and ready for shipment. The remaining two buildings are expected to be completed and shipped in January 2027.

Engineering and fabrication of the conveyor systems is progressing well. Initial conveyor deliveries are expected to begin arriving on site in mid-December, with additional conveyors being manufactured and shipped in priority sequence throughout the first quarter of 2027.

Taken together, these achievements represent substantial progress toward delivery of one of the Company's most important infrastructure projects. The project continues to transition from planning into full-scale execution with detailed engineering, procurement, and construction activities advancing simultaneously.

The Sorting Facility remains on schedule for operational readiness in the second quarter of 2027, with full commissioning anticipated during July-August 2027. Pre-commissioning activities will involve sorting existing stockpile inventory, providing an opportunity to validate system performance ahead of full scale operations. Once operational, the Sorting Facility will process run-of-mine material and is expected to enhance gold grades while eliminating dilution prior to trucking and shipping, improve operating efficiencies, reduce transportation costs, and strengthen project economics.

Terry Harbort, President and CEO, stated, "We are very pleased with the progress being made on the Sorting Facility. With key infrastructure completed, major equipment secured, and construction activities continuing to ramp up, the project remains on schedule for operational readiness in Q2 2027. This Sorting Facility represents an important milestone for Bralorne and will play a significant role in improving operational efficiency and supporting the Company's long-term growth objectives."

Figure 1: Aerial view of the Mustang Mine site with a rendered overlay of the sorting facility. The recently completed machine shop and the Mustang Mine power generation systems are shown to scale in their actual locations. The Sorting Facility rendering is provided for conceptual illustration only and may not be to scale. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence from 1 through 4.

Figure 2: 3D rendering of the Sorting Facility. The product sorting process flow is indicated by the gold arrows, with major sorting equipment labelled in sequence. Run-of-mine material is loaded into the jaw crusher (1) via the loading ramp and conveyed to the triple-deck screening plant (2). Screened material is then transported to the TOMRA XRT sorter (3), where gold-bearing material is separated from waste rock. The sorted product is conveyed to the cone crusher (4) before being stockpiled within a covered tension-fabric storage building. Waste reject material is conveyed to a separate waste stockpile.

Figure 3: Mustang Mine and Sorting Facility Power Generation System will power all Mustang Operations including the ore sorter, with 100% redundancy.

Figure 4: Left, the Mustang Mine and Sorter Facility power generation system in the foreground, and the new tension-fabric steel frame mechanic shop in the centre background. Right, the new Mustang Mine Mechanic shop.

Figure 5: The Jaw Crusher, Cone Crusher, vibrating screen plant and all crushing circuit equipment frames arrived in Bralorne in October. Installation of the crushing circuit is expected to commence in Q1 2027.

data.title: South Korean shares fall as hawkish Fed dents risk sentiment
data.description:
Key points:
  • KOSPI falls, foreigners net sellers
  • Korean won strengthens against dollar
  • South Korea benchmark bond yield falls

Round-up of South Korean financial markets:

** South Korean shares fell more than 1% on Thursday after hawkish remarks from US Federal Reserve officials reinforced expectations that interest rates could stay higher for longer.

** The benchmark KOSPI was down 55.85 points, or 1.10%, at 5,011.59, as of 0156 GMT.

** Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 meeting showed on Wednesday.

** Fed governor Christopher Waller said the US central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation that he fears is changing public psychology about prices, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of hikes in 2027.

** "The domestic market is falling on Nvidia cutting earlier gains overnight, pressure from hawkish comments by Fed officials and caution over Anthropic's IPO," said Han Ji-young, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities.

** Anthropic's IPO raised $81.31 billion on Wednesday, eclipsing SpaceX's offering to claim the title of the largest market debut on record.

** Shares of South Korean chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 1.64%, while peer SK Hynix lost 0.52%.

** Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 2.62%, while Hyundai Motor and sister automaker Kia Corp were down 2.43% and 1.84%, respectively.

** Steelmaker POSCO Holdings shed 1.53%, while drugmaker Samsung BioLogics fell 1.76%.

** Of the total 904 traded issues, 336 shares advanced, while 536 declined.

** Foreigners were net sellers of shares worth 162.6 billion won ($122.02 million).

** The won was quoted at 1,330.7 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform , 0.23% higher than its previous close at 1,333.7.

** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell 1.4 basis points to 3.732%, while the benchmark 10-year yield fell 1.0 basis points to 3.953%.

data.title: Conveyor collapse kills three at India's NTPC Tandwa plant
data.description:
At least three workers were killed and four others were injured after a coal conveyor structure collapsed at NTPC's Tandwa project in Chatra district, Jharkhand, The New Indian Express reported on November 18.

The accident occurred at the plant's external Coal Handling Plant (CHP), where a section of the conveyor system gave way, trapping workers beneath the debris. Preliminary findings point to a possible structural design flaw in the conveyor belt system, although the exact cause of the collapse has yet to be established.

The project involved two external contractors. NTPC had awarded the conveyor belt construction contract to ThyssenKrupp, which subsequently engaged Simplex as a sub-contractor to execute the work, according to the newspaper.

Witnesses said the incident took place near Junction No. 1 of the conveyor system when a take-up trolley collapsed, striking workers in the vicinity.

Chatra Superintendent of Police Animesh Naithani confirmed that three workers had died in the accident. He said Tandwa police station officer-in-charge Vipin Kumar had reached the site with a police team soon after receiving information about the incident. Police personnel, administrative officials and rescue teams remained at the location as relief and rescue operations continued.

The accident prompted an immediate response from local authorities and NTPC's plant management, with rescue efforts launched to locate and assist those trapped in the wreckage.

The four injured workers were taken to NTPC Sanjeevani Hospital in Tandwa, where they are receiving medical treatment.

One of the deceased was identified as Rajendra Soni, also known as Raju, a resident of Tandwa. He had been associated with the company since 2019.

data.title: BOJ chief offers upbeat view on consumption despite recent weakness
data.description:
By Leika Kihara

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda said on Thursday consumption would likely recover after a temporary slowdown, adding that the drop in private spending seen in third-quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data was within the central bank's expectations.

"Nominal wages will rise steadily, while the pace of inflation is likely to gradually slow," Ueda told parliament, adding that rising household income would underpin consumption.

He also said consumption was resilient as a whole, with the drop seen in third-quarter GDP data resulting from rising cost of living and bad weather.

"We expect consumption to resume a moderate uptrend," he said, suggesting that soft third-quarter consumption alone would not prevent the BOJ from raising rates again in the near-term.

Ueda signalled the BOJ's vigilance to the inflationary impact of the weak yen, saying the currency's falls may cause an inflation overshoot by boosting prices for a wide range of goods.

"We are mindful of the risk that rising crude oil prices and yen declines, if they persist, could hurt households' real income and weigh on consumption more than expected," Ueda said.

On monetary policy, Ueda reiterated the central bank's resolve to keep raising interest rates, saying financial conditions remain loose despite past hikes.

"It's important to anchor underlying inflation around our 2% target to avoid risk of an inflation overshoot from materialising and hurting the economy," he said.

A majority of analysts polled by Reuters expect the BOJ to raise interest rates in December and follow up with another by end-March, as the central bank remains focused on inflation and a weak currency.

data.title: iA Financial Group Announces Offering of $500 million of 4.625% Fixed/Floating Unsecured Subordinated Debentures
data.description:
iA Financial Group (the “Company”) () announced today an offering of $500 million aggregate principal amount of 4.625% fixed/floating unsecured subordinated debentures (the “Debentures”) due November 24, 2036 (the “Offering”).

The Debentures will be issued as “Sustainable Bonds” under iA Financial Group’s 2026 Sustainability Bond Framework, published on November 17, 2026 (the “Framework”). The Framework is available on the Company’s website at ia.ca.

The Offering is expected to close on or about November 24, 2026. The Company intends to use an amount equal to the net proceeds from the sale of the Debentures to finance or re-finance, in part or in full, new and/or existing Eligible Assets within each of the Green Eligible Categories and Social Eligible Categories, all as defined in the Framework.

The Debentures will mature on November 24, 2036. Interest on the Debentures at the rate of 4.625% per annum will be payable in arrears in equal semi-annual installments on May 24 and November 24, in each year, commencing on May 24, 2027 and continuing until November 24, 2031. From November 24, 2031, interest on the Debentures will be payable at a rate per annum equal to Daily Compounded CORRA, plus 1.27% payable quarterly in arrears on the 24th day of each of February, May, August and November in each year, commencing on February 24, 2032.

The Offering is being done on a best efforts agency basis by a syndicate of agents led by National Bank of Canada Capital Markets, RBC Capital Markets and Scotiabank as co-leads and bookrunners, and including BMO Capital Markets, CIBC Capital Markets, TD Securities, iA Private Wealth Inc., Casgrain & Company Limited, Morgan Stanley Canada Limited and UBS Investment Bank. National Bank of Canada Capital Markets also acted as Sustainability Structuring Advisor on the Framework.

The Debentures will be offered in each of the provinces of Canada under a shelf prospectus supplement (the “Prospectus Supplement”) to the Company’s short form base shelf prospectus dated May 12, 2026 (the “Shelf Prospectus”).

Access to the Prospectus Supplement, the Shelf Prospectus and any amendments to the documents is provided in accordance with securities legislation relating to procedures for providing access to a shelf prospectus supplement, a base shelf prospectus and any amendment to the documents.
